description: Participants assemble an analysis dataset for a fictional food bank network from four sources: registrations with personal data, branch logs, a donations API and open population data. They record provenance, join with key and cardinality checks, clean Arabic and English text, dates and units, write validation rules that rerun on every build, and measure how missing data and measurement error move a headline estimate. Personal data are minimised and pseudonymised, and the dataset rebuilds from raw sources with one command.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-106 Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom
Writes SQL joins and group-by queries without assistance

outcomes.text: Describe missing-data mechanisms and kinds of measurement error and the bias each can introduce, given six scenarios from the case
outcomes.evidence: mechanism and bias direction for each, at least five of six correct

outcomes.text: Prepare a provenance record per source covering origin, owner, coverage, sharing basis, refresh date and limits, given the four sources and their documentation
outcomes.evidence: a provenance file that passes a reviewer's checklist

outcomes.text: Implement joins with key checks, cardinality tests and reconciliation counts so that no row is silently lost or duplicated, given tables with seeded duplicate, missing and mistyped keys
outcomes.evidence: a join log of row counts per step and set-aside rows with reasons

outcomes.text: Configure validation rules for types, ranges, uniqueness, completeness and cross-field consistency that run on every rebuild, given the joined table and its data dictionary
outcomes.evidence: a rule suite that passes on the clean build and fails readably on a corrupted batch

outcomes.text: Analyse how complete-case analysis, imputation and a sensitivity range change a headline estimate, given parcels per eligible household by district, with 18% of household sizes missing
outcomes.evidence: a comparison table and a recommended estimate with its reason

outcomes.text: Build a rebuildable analysis dataset from raw sources with personal data minimised and pseudonymised, given a question set by the food bank and the four raw sources
outcomes.evidence: a repository that rebuilds with one command, with provenance, rules and quality report, defended live
